sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the area between the northern shoulder of the Peloritani Mts. (southwest) and Aeolian Is. (north), right at the termination of the extensional axis of the southern Apennines. This source is a near-vertical, SW-dipping, right-lateral strike-slip fault, that possibly belongs to the strike-slip system that dissects and advances the central and southern Calabrian arc toward SE.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a sparse intermediate (4.5 < Mw < 5.5) seismicity all over this region, including the damaging earthquakes that hit the southern sector of the source on 10 March 1786 (Mw 6.0, Sicilia Nord-orientale) and on 15 April 1978 (Mw 6.1, Golfo di Patti).
The Tindari Fault System (or "Tindari-Letojanni Line") is a NNW-trending fault set that runs from the northern shoulder of the Mt. Etna volcano to the Aeolian Islands. This fault system has been relatively well studied over the years and is thought to be an oblique dextral structure. Given its position at the boundary between extension in the Messina Straits (to the east) compression (to the west) and the key earthquakes that have occurred in the area, we believe that this structure holds a key seismogenic potential. It is also possible that this region is actively controlled by the south-easterly advancement of the Calabrian Arc toward the Ionian Sea.
A segment of this Source has been associated with the 1978 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenic processes in this region, the reader may refer to the relevant Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped regional structures. Also the dip was based on geological and geometrical considerations. Rake is indicative of normal to right-lateral strike-slip faulting, based on regional geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
